rescan.name: fdps_move_grid_mark_zone_of_control
rescan.note:
Not settled, but materially narrowed and recorded. The single concern (emit + review copies of it, both left status "open", their `what`/`needs` untouched, a `rescan` field added to each and the review copy pointed at the emit copy with `same_as`) is: how the four neighbour marks in 00010c30 were spelled in the original source.

What the neighbours' verdicts gave. The first branch of `needs` — the emit of fdps_move_grid_set_stop_flag @ 00010da0 — has now run and is exhausted: 00010da0.emit.json and 00010da0.review.json are present, approved, with zero open_issues, and neither recovers the spelling. It did turn one assumption into a measurement: 00010da0's frame is SUB ESP,0x4, one dword local (the cell pointer), coordinates read straight from [EBP+0x14]/[EBP+0x18] with no temporaries. Re-walking 00010c30 myself, its 0x5c frame decomposes exactly with no gap — three function-scope dwords (grid_width [EBP-0x8], grid_height [EBP-0x4], centre cell pointer [EBP-0xc]) plus four disjoint five-dword groups in source order (left -0x10..-0x20, up -0x24..-0x34, right -0x38..-0x48, down -0x4c..-0x5c), each group being cell pointer, live x, live y, copied-from y, copied-from x. Five dwords per site is two more than the primitive's body plus one parameter binding would need, so the extra pair is real: whatever the spelling, it binds the coordinates twice or binds an aggregate.

Two candidates eliminated. (1) It is not 00010da0's body with its parameters bound once. (2) It is not 00010de0's idiom: fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range @ 00010de0, the four-direction fill in the same translation unit under the same flags, also expands one body four times but writes the SAME slots at all four sites (-0x8, -0xc, -0x18, -0x34, -0x44 at 00010f3f, 00011087, 000111d4, 00011315), where 00010c30 gives each site a fresh group — a difference in source, not codegen. That was the "same double-temporary pattern elsewhere" lead the entry named; checked at the strongest candidate, negative. I also checked the prequel per CLAUDE.md: fd2-anatomy has no movement-grid material at all (only a workspace/ hit, not citable).

What remains, and its limit. Only the wcc386 10.0a experiment. It can decide the binding structure (two nested bindings vs a two-int aggregate — different declarations, and -od gives every declared object its own slot); it cannot decide macro vs four hand-written copies, because after preprocessing those are the same token stream, so no reading of FDPS.LE and no rebuild comparison can ever separate them. Recorded so that half is not left standing as if a later ticket will close it.

The stake the entry named is closed: it said the answer "can change how movegrid.c reads once 00010da0 is emitted alongside it". Both are now in src/movegrid.c, 00010da0 emitted whole with a header comment stating the relationship, reviewed and approved side by side.

No blocking finding. The emitted C is unchanged and correct either way; no equivalence question is open and no code was touched. Ghidra was read only — no rename, prototype, comment or label written. rescan.name: fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles

rescan.name: fdps_saf_get_frame
rescan.note: Both entries for 000140e0 (emitter + reviewer, the same concern) settled and committed as faccc6e. The concern was never about this function's equivalence -- it was the coordination question of whether a #pragma pack(1) .SAF header struct should go into fdpstype.h or whether byte-offset addressing stays the house style, and it was unanswerable when the sibling readers did not exist. They do now. All three descriptor readers in saf.c (000140e0, fdps_saf_frame_count 000144e0, fdps_saf_advance_tick 00014550, the last writing the count read and frame lookup out inline again) use the same two #defines SAF_FRAME_COUNT_OFFSET 0x0c / SAF_FRAME_SECTION_START_OFFSET 0x0e. The decisive evidence is the reader in a different file, where the style could actually have diverged: fdps_sfx_play at 000142d0 in audio.c reads the sound descriptor at +0x2a/+0x2c and independently spelled it as byte offsets, its file comment citing src/saf.h for the reason, and neither its emit nor its review verdict raises the header-struct question at all -- the second emitter met a decision already made. Two things hold it in place: src/fdpstype.h still contains no SAF type (so there is no struct to include by accident), and src/saf.h's file comment states the rule in prose in the header every later SAF reader must include. No code change is owed and there is no blocking finding: re-read against the assembly this round (000140f5 MOV AX,word ptr [EAX+0xc] / 000140f9 AND EAX,0xffff, then 00014118 ADD EDX,dword ptr [EAX+0xe] -- a zero-extended u16 and a 32-bit load two bytes after it), the emitted C is exact, and it would have been exact under either style. Recorded once: the emitter entry carries answer/settled_by/residual, the reviewer entry carries same_as pointing at it. Residual noted inside the entry rather than left as an open concern: the tilemap and tile descriptors at +0x16 and +0x20 have no emitted reader yet (fdps_saf_play_over_background 0001ecf0 and fdps_saf_play_over_scene 000222c0 are routed but not emitted), so the chosen style has not been exercised there -- but that is a rule those functions' own emit and review will apply, not a question hanging off this one. Three sources read for 000140e0 (plate comment, disassembly, decompiled C); no Ghidra write of any kind; nothing dirty outside tools/code_emit/data/, and the tree is clean after the commit.

rescan.name: fdps_sfx_play
rescan.note: Settled the AIL flags-word concern; the playtest concern stays open untouched. No neighbour verdict was relevant -- fdps_sfx_play's only caller (fdps_draw_composite_sprite @ 00014140) has no verdict file yet and all eight callees are vendor AIL entry points, so the answer came from AIL's own code, read-only. Searching the whole image for reads of SAMPLE+0x38 (the field AIL_internal_set_sample_type_inner writes at 000472ee from AIL_set_sample_type's third argument) finds three: 00045fe6 TEST byte ptr [EBX+0x38],0x1 in AIL_internal_build_sample_volume_tables, and 00054594 TEST dword ptr [ECX+0x38],0x2 plus 000545c0 TEST dword ptr [ECX+0x38],0x1 in AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample, which builds the mixer-variant index it CALLs through at 0x52a5c. The bit-1 test sits inside the stereo branch: 00054585/0005458b compare the sample format field against 2 and 3 and JNZ straight to 000545a0, so for a non-stereo sample bit 1 is never read at all; only in the stereo path does 00054591 OR EAX,0x2 run and 0005459d OR EAX,0x4 pick a different stereo mix loop. So bit 1 is a stereo-only mixer-variant selector (consistent with Miles' channel-order flag, but that name is not what the binary proves and was not adopted), and bit 0 is the signed-PCM flag. For fdps_sfx_play the literal 2 is inert -- all 608 .SAF clips are mono 8-bit, format 0 -- and the emitted C already pushes the same literal the original does at 00014445, so this is NOT a blocking finding and no code change is called for. Recorded one non-blocking residual: the comment above AIL_SAMPLE_TYPE_FLAGS in src/audio.c still says nothing about bit 1, which is not wrong, just improvable by whoever next opens that file for a real reason. The second concern (the tests observe what is handed to AIL, not the audible result; loop count 1 is indistinguishable from AIL_init_sample's own default written at 00047239) is left exactly as it was -- it needs the DOSBox-X playtest it already names, and no neighbour's contract can supply it. Only tools/code_emit/data/emit_issues.json changed; committed as 24f857b, working tree clean.

rescan.name: fdps_free_global_resource_buffers
rescan.note:
Settled the declared-type concern (emit entry 2, with the review's duplicate pointed at it via same_as). Its stated precondition -- "table.c's accessors emitted" -- is now met: all nine are emitted with approved verdicts (00018ab0 character_base, 00018ae0 growth, 00018b10 enemy, 00018b40 item, 00018b70 class, 00018ba0 class_equip, 00018bd0 spell_effect, 00018c00 spell_learn, 00018c30 promotion; the entry's "00018b80"/"00018be0" were slips). A read-only get_xrefs_to on each of the nine globals (00063fd0..00063ff0) returns the same four references every time -- two fdps_load_data_tables immediates, this function's READ, and exactly one accessor's READ -- so the reader set is closed and no later reader can want a different declaration. The readers settle it against retyping: each accessor is (struct X *)(global + index * <file stride literal>), byte arithmetic on the byte pointer. Retyping the global to a record pointer would scale by sizeof(struct X), which is not the stride -- struct fdps_spell_effect is a short plus five unsigned chars (wcc386 sizes it 8) against MAGICDAT.DAT's stride 7, and 0x0b growth / 0x17 item are the same trap -- so a struct-typed global would silently change every computed address. gamedata.h keeps unsigned char *; no code change, nothing blocking.

Still open, unchanged and untouched: whether the shutdown path can be entered twice, which would make this function's nine unguarded frees a nine-way double free. What is missing is exactly what the entry says -- fdps_shutdown_free_resources @ 00029440 and main @ 00029220 are not emitted and have no verdict files, and neither does the fatal-error exit path, so there is no neighbour judgement to use. Deciding it would mean reading two unemitted functions in full and forming the judgement their own emit round owns, so it was left alone rather than manufactured.

Settlement recorded in tools/code_emit/data/emit_issues.json under key 00018a20 and committed alone (0af06f6). Working tree clean; no Ghidra writes, no src/ or tests/ edits.

rescan.name: fdps_get_character_base_record
rescan.note:
兩個獨立疑慮結案（各含 emitter 與 reviewer 各一則，共 4 筆 entry 轉為 resolved；reviewer 那兩筆用 same_as 指回 emitter 的，結論只寫一份），一則仍 open，原文一字未動。

結案一：呼叫端會不會用越界的 char_id 進來。鄰居 verdict workspace/code_emit/verdicts/00023bc0.emit.json（fdps_roster_add_character）現在存在，正是原本說「要等它 emit」的那支。它自己沒有邊界檢查，因為根本不需要：get_xrefs_to(00023bc0) 給出 12 個 caller、24 個呼叫點，我逐一 disassemble 過每一個 caller（00020e90/00020ef0/00020f30/00020f70/00021030/00021070/000210b0/00021140/00021240/00021350/00021490/0002ac10），24 個位置**全部**是 PUSH 立即數，值域 0x00–0x0c，最大 12。名冊路徑的 char_id 是編譯期常數，不存在任何由選單、腳本或表格算出來的 id。另一條路徑 fdps_deploy_unit 的 CMP 0x3c 本來就看得到。所以「讀過表尾」在原版不可達，src/table.c 與 tests/table.c 不必改，an_id_past_the_end_is_not_clamped 也照舊——它釘的是這支 accessor 本身的行為。非 blocking。順帶記進 residual：fdps_title_demo 會加入 id 0x0c，那是 assets/characters.md 說的樣板列而非真人物，但在界內、不是邊界問題，歸 0002ac10 自己 emit 時處理。

結案二：表是不是真的 60 筆。這則不必等 VFS reader，數字早就量過而且在正典裡：resource_info/vfs.md 的 MISC.VFS 成員表寫 FRIAPRDA.DAT = 1,440 byte，resource_info/data_tables.md 記 1,440 / 24 = 60，且明說九張 .DAT 沒有 header／magic／筆數欄位，record 從成員第一個 byte 起連續排列，所以筆數就是大小除以 stride，1440 / 0x18 = 60 整除無餘。同樣用肖像編號索引的 FRILEVUP.DAT（660/11）與 GETMGTAB.DAT（720/12）也都是 60，是獨立的旁證。兩份都是進版控的正典頁，不是 workspace 產物。

仍 open（reviewer 的第三則，原文未動）：兩個呼叫端對 record 五個 16-bit 基礎值的延伸方式不一致——fdps_roster_add_character 用 MOVSX（00023c2a 等五處），fdps_deploy_unit 零延伸（0002356b/0002356f、0002359e、000235aa、000235b6），而 src/fdpstype.h 宣告為 signed short，只重現名冊那條。缺的那一半現在只剩一個：roster 側已隨 00023bc0 落地並在其 verdict 的 contract C 釘死為有號，但 fdps_deploy_unit @ 000232b0 在 emit_state.json 裡是 null（未 emit、無 verdict），所以「deploy 路徑的 AND 0xffff 到底是欄位本身無號，還是那個運算式上的 cast」仍無從判定。這不是這支函式能回答的——它從不解參考該 record。沒有捏造結論。

Ghidra 全程唯讀（get_function_callers / get_xrefs_to / get_function_by_address / disassemble_function），沒有任何寫入，也沒有失敗或逾時。改動只有 tools/code_emit/data/emit_issues.json 一檔，已用 pathspec 單獨 commit（a19908d），工作樹乾淨。

rescan.name: fdps_get_enemy_record
rescan.note:
Neither concern is settled; emit_issues.json is untouched and nothing was committed (working tree clean). What I did read, with three sources on each caller I touched.

Concern 1 (does the side-byte guard imply portrait_id >= 0x3c) is NARROWED but still open. Neighbour verdicts pin the side byte's meaning: 000118f0 (fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles) and 00010b90 record that a player unit's own side byte is 2 and that side_select is a truth value, i.e. side 0 is the enemy side. 00023bc0 (fdps_roster_add_character) is the only emitted writer of the side/portrait pair and it stamps side 2 at 00023c76 with portrait_id = char_id at 00023c7a/00023c83, so the roster-enrolment path can never produce a side-0 record at all -- one candidate writer is off the list. I also re-read both damage callers in Ghidra and confirmed the accessor is fed by the side-0 record itself at both: 00028460 tests [EBP-0x20]+0x6 == 0 at 000284f7 and takes +0x7 of that same record at 00028500; 00019f80 tests attacker [EBP-0x50]+0x6 == 2 at 0001a2ce and defender [EBP-0x4c]+0x6 == 0 at 0001a2de, then takes +0x7 of the DEFENDER at 0001a2e9 -- so no side-2 record ever reaches the SUB 0x3c. Still missing, and it is exactly what the entry already names: fdps_deploy_unit 000232b0 and fdps_build_map_unit_array 00022be0 are still unemitted (no verdict files), so nothing yet shows whether any path can leave a side-0 unit with an id below 0x3c. Entry left verbatim.

Concern 2 (are the 91 records all real) is also still open. No neighbour verdict touches ENEMYDAT.DAT's contents; 00022e30 and 00023050 are archive/CEL loaders, not the table read. Out of curiosity I looked at the project's existing extraction, workspace/vfs_dump/MISC/ENEMYDAT.DAT: it is 910 bytes, 91 stride-10 records, none zero-filled, and records 57..90 (bar 68) are one repeated default pattern 01 02 12 00 00 05 02 01 04 1e -- the ITEM.DAT shape of a filled tail rather than 34 distinct enemies. I did NOT record that as a settlement: it answers only the storage half, the entry's own "needs" asks for the file through the emitted VFS reader plus the table's decoding (resource_info/data_tables.md still marks it 尚未解讀), and the operative unknown -- the highest portrait id the game can actually produce -- is map data, not this file. Passing the observation up rather than writing a half-conclusion into the entry.

No blocking finding: the emitted C is a pure base + index * 10 accessor and neither concern bears on its equivalence. No Ghidra writes were made.
